data.name: Lucelia
data.gender_notes: Lucelia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Lucelia is derived from the Latin word lucere, meaning 'to shine, light up, or be clear'. The name was traditionally given to girls born during the Christmas season, symbolizing the light of the Christ child. The name Lucelia carries the meaning “Light, brightness” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Lucelia usually hope their child will grow to embody light, brightness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Lucelia is often seen as a reminder of the light of Christ, and is associated with hope, joy, and renewal.
data.etymology: Lucelia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Light, brightness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lucelia total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: לוסליה
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא האור שלי, אור האל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: לוסליה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו במילה העברית 'לוא' שמשמעותה 'אור', ו'אליה' שמשמעותה 'אלוהים הוא אור'. השם לוסליה משלב את שני המרכיבים ומשמעותו 'אלוהים הוא האור שלי' או 'אור האל'. השם מופיע במסורת הנוצרית כסמל לאור האלוהים המנחה את המאמינים.

in_greek.name: Λουκελία
in_greek.long_meaning: Η Λουκελία είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'λουκός' που σημαίνει 'φως' και 'ελία' που σημαίνει 'Θεός'. Η Λουκελία συμβολίζει το φως του Θεού και αποτελεί ένδειξη της καθοδήγησης του Θεού για τους πιστούς.

in_latin.name: Lucelia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Lucelia originem ducit a verbis Latinis 'lux' quae significat 'lux' et 'Dei' quae significat 'Dei'. Lucelia igitur significat 'Dei lux' vel 'lux divina', quae est symbolum luminis divini quod fideles ducit.

in_english.name: Lucelia
in_english.meaning: God is my light, divine light
in_english.long_meaning: The name Lucelia is of Christian origin, derived from the Hebrew and Greek roots meaning 'light' and 'God'. It signifies 'God is my light' or 'divine light', symbolizing the guidance and illumination that comes from God. Historically, the name reflects the biblical theme of God as the light of His people, as seen in Psalm 27:1, 'The Lord is my light and my salvation.' In Christian tradition, Lucelia represents spiritual enlightenment and divine protection.

data.spiritual_significance: The name Lucelia signifies the inner light of the soul. It is a reminder of the divine presence within each of us, illuminating our path in life and helping us to see the world around us with clarity and understanding.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lucelia: Derived from the Latin word "lux," meaning light, and "celia," meaning heaven. The name Lucelia symbolizes a radiant soul, shining brightly from the divine heavens above. It represents a strong connection to the divine and an enlightened spirit.

historical_references.reference: Lucelia was a name given to several early Christian saints. The most famous was Lucilia of Syracuse, who was martyred during the Diocletian Persecution around 311 AD. She is venerated as a virgin and martyr, and her remains are believed to be enshrined at the Monastery of Santa Lucia al Mare in Sicily.

historical_references.context: Martyr and Virgin, enshrined in Sicily

historical_references.reference: Lucelia of Rome, also known as Lucilia of the Carthaginian Martyrs, was a Christian martyr who was martyred during the Valerian Persecution around 258 AD. She was a Roman woman who was condemned to be thrown into a pit of wild animals for her faith, but she was miraculously saved. Her name is included in the Martyrology of Jerome, and she is venerated as a saint in the Roman Catholic Church.

historical_references.context: Martyr, saved from wild animals, venerated in Roman Catholic Church
